name: 80s PWM string pad: pulse wave with free-running (seconds-based) LFO on pulse width, slight osc-2 detune, slow attack/release, static filter
goal: Build a classic 1980s string pad from an init patch: switch the oscillator from saw to pulse, modulate pulse width from an LFO set in seconds (free-running, ~0.7, not tempo-synced so the ensemble rate never changes with song tempo), blend a second oscillator ever so slightly detuned, low-pass to remove the very high end with the filter envelope and other filter mod sources switched off, slow fade-in attack and long release — a dedicated PWM string pad distinct from our PW drone and unison string-section skills.

source.title: 80s String Pad Tutorial (1/2) - Pulse Width Modulation in Tyrell N6

prerequisites: Two-oscillator subtractive synth with pulse wave + PW modulation (or Web Audio PeriodicWave/pulse via two offset saws)
constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Values are the presenter's display units, set by ear ('use your ears'); treat as starting points.
Reverb and EQ are covered in the follow-up video (not this transcript).
Web Audio: PWM can be made by subtracting a phase-shifted saw from a saw and modulating the delay/offset with an LFO (implementation note).

steps.action: Start from an init patch; keep a scope visible. Change oscillator 1 from saw to pulse (square = 50% duty cycle; pulse widths roughly 10–90% duty).
steps.expect: Hollow square tone; scope shows pulse

steps.action: Route an LFO to pulse width and watch the scope: the pulse width sweeps.
Switch the PW LFO from tempo-sync to free-running seconds so the string movement keeps the same rate regardless of DAW tempo; set ~0.7 and a moderate depth.
Bring in oscillator 2 (presenter's level ~17.5) alongside osc 1, then detune osc 2 ever so slightly (fine ~0.20) — perfectly in-tune oscillators lose the effect.
Lower the low-pass cutoff to cut the really high end; reduce output level if hot.
Amp envelope: much slower attack (presenter ~38 display units) for a fade-in and a long release that tails naturally.
steps.expect: Pad fades in and rings out smoothly

steps.action: Set master transpose from −12 to 0 so A440 plays A440. Turn off the filter envelope and other filter modulation sources so the filter stays static.
steps.expect: Correct pitch; no filter 'wah' on note-on

steps.action: Set the voice/unison count the presenter uses (2), play chords to confirm the 1980s string pad, and save it as a patch.

verification: Scope shows pulse width moving when the LFO is active.
Changing DAW tempo does not change the PWM rate.
Setting osc-2 detune back to 0 noticeably flattens the pad.
Notes fade in and release slowly with no filter envelope sweep.
